flags.subject: Single-entry status
flags.finding: Not one Strip event in this dataset has an official source that confirms a single entry / no re-entry limit.
flags.detail: The Venetian DSE IV structure sheets that were opened (14 of 37) set the buy-in, fee split, starting chips, level length and late-registration close, and they restrict play after a player bags chips for Day 2 — but none of them states a maximum number of entries, a no-re-entry rule or a no-add-on rule. The remaining 23 Venetian sheets were not opened and are treated as unverified. Wynn, Bellagio and Caesars Palace all state re-entry or rebuy/add-on mechanics in their own terms.
flags.action: Do not label any event 'single-entry confirmed'. Ask each poker room, in writing, for the maximum-entry rule per event before booking.

flags.subject: 8 AM start
flags.finding: No verified Strip tournament starts at 8:00 AM, so the requested 8 AM all-day schedule cannot be built from official sources.
flags.detail: Earliest verified starts: Caesars Palace 10:00 AM (official flyer), Venetian 10:10 AM (official schedule). Horseshoe is listed at 9:00 AM but only on a Caesars editorial page, not the room's own flyer. Wynn, Bellagio and MGM Grand all start at 11:00–12:00.
flags.action: Either accept a 10:00 AM start or verify the Horseshoe 9 AM slot with the room directly.

flags.subject: Dated hotel totals
flags.finding: No dated checkout total exists anywhere in this dataset.
flags.detail: The Venetian booking calendar and the Caesars booking flow return '$XXX' placeholders to a non-browser client, and the Wynn room pages return a 'page has checked out' stub. The published $119 / $209 figures are starting rates conditional on six hours of play per night, not quotes.
flags.action: A human has to open each booking page in a browser, pick the exact dates, and capture the checkout total, the nightly average, the fee and tax lines and the cancellation deadline.

flags.subject: Venetian poker-rate mapping
flags.finding: The Venice/Palazzo poker-rate page prints '$119 and $209' without saying which property gets which number.
flags.detail: Wording: 'These rates will start as low as $119 and $209 and can be higher.' Both properties are named in the preceding sentence, so the mapping is ambiguous. Earlier dashboards in this repo assigned $119 to the Venetian and $209 to the Palazzo; that assignment is an inference.
flags.action: Confirm the mapping by phone (866.255.8936, code EPOKR25) before using either figure.

flags.subject: Bellagio Saturday buy-in
flags.finding: The official Saturday Bellagio PDF contradicts itself: titled '$1100 BUY-IN' but its rules say 'Of the $600 Buy-in, $510 goes to the Prize Pool'.
flags.detail: Both statements are in the same official document. The $1,100 headline and the $600 fee split cannot both be right.
flags.action: Treat the Saturday buy-in as unverified; confirm with the Bellagio poker room (702.693.7291).

flags.subject: MGM Grand schedule month label
flags.finding: The MGM Grand weekly schedule PDF is headed 'MGM Grand August Tournament Schedule' and is not dated otherwise.
flags.detail: The daily times (11:10am / 7:10pm / 11:10pm) match the live MGM Grand poker page, but the PDF itself may be an August edition still being served in November.
flags.action: Confirm with the MGM Grand poker room (702.891.7434) that the times are current.

flags.subject: Horseshoe schedule source
flags.finding: Horseshoe's six daily start times appear only on a Caesars editorial article, not the poker room's own flyer.
flags.detail: caesars.com/las-vegas/explore/... lists 9 a.m., 11 a.m., 2 p.m., 5 p.m., 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. No Horseshoe buy-in, guarantee, structure or entry rule could be retrieved, and the direct PDF guesses returned empty documents.
flags.action: Ask the Horseshoe poker room for its current flyer before relying on any Horseshoe row.

flags.subject: Caesars Palace resort fee
flags.finding: No official Caesars page would render a resort-fee figure.
flags.detail: caesars.com/caesars-palace/hotel/resort-fee redirects to the hotel landing page. Third-party trackers quote $54.95 + tax; that number is deliberately NOT entered in the hotel table.

flags.action: None needed; walking time between the two towers is included in the walking table.

flags.subject: Wynn WPT $160 nightly / $200 daily add-ons
flags.finding: Every Wynn daily event carries a paid add-on or re-entries, so none qualifies as single-entry.
flags.detail: Mon–Thu $200: re-entry allowed. Fri $240: 'Re-entry is NOT allowed' but unlimited $200 rebuys and one $100 add-on. Sat/Sun $200: re-entries plus one add-on per entry. Nightly $160: re-entries plus one add-on per entry.
flags.action: Treat the whole Wynn daily slate as spend-more. It is shown on the spend-more page, not the single-entry page.

flags.subject: Walking times are point-to-point
flags.finding: The walking minutes come from Google Maps' routing between property pins, not from a published casino-floor route.
flags.detail: Google Maps is a routing service, not an official property source, and its pin for a property is not necessarily the lobby door. Times also do not include the walk from the hotel room to the lobby.
flags.action: Treat every walk time as a floor, not a guaranteed measure, and add 5–10 minutes of building-internal walking.

flags.subject: Same-day multi-tournament assumption
flags.finding: No source publishes a finish time for any event, so a two-tournament day cannot be verified.
flags.detail: The schedule publishes start times and late-registration cut-offs only. The 'derived maximum length' used on the Day Plan page is arithmetic on the published structure (levels × level length + breaks), not a published finish time.
flags.action: Use the day plan as a primary event plus a conditional fallback, never as a guaranteed double.

flags.subject: Repo contains four overlapping dashboards
flags.finding: Before this consolidation the repository published four separate dashboards at /, /pages/, /docs/ and /verified/, with overlapping and sometimes conflicting numbers.
flags.detail: They were built by earlier parallel sessions. Their files are preserved under archive/ and are no longer linked from the main navigation.
flags.action: Review the archived copies if any number looks different from what you remember. This dashboard supersedes them.

questions.question: What are the exact trip dates and the number of nights?
questions.known: The verified Strip calendar runs Nov 16 – Dec 23, 2026 (Venetian DSE IV) and Nov 27 – Dec 21 (Wynn WPT).
questions.missing: Nothing in the repo fixes a stay window. Room totals, walk-day routing and event choices are all date-specific.
questions.how_to_close: Pick a 7-night window inside Nov 25 – Dec 23, 2026 (the only window where two properties both publish schedules).
questions.affects: Hotel cost, trip cost, day plan

questions.question: Is a maximum of one entry per event actually required, and would the player accept a re-entry event if it were cheap?
questions.known: Zero events are confirmed single-entry. Every property that states a rule states re-entry, rebuy or a paid add-on.
questions.missing: Whether the user's 'single entry only' rule is hard (never play a re-entry event) or soft (prefer single-entry, accept a capped event).
questions.how_to_close: Answer the constraint question. If hard, the dataset yields no bookable event and the trip is not possible on official information.

questions.question: What is the maximum total buy-in per day and for the trip?
questions.known: Verified buy-ins in the window range from $100 (Caesars Palace daily) to $25,800 (Wynn High Roller).
questions.missing: No bankroll or per-day cap was supplied, so the ranking cannot apply a cost ceiling.
questions.how_to_close: State a per-day and a trip maximum.

questions.question: What hotel quality floor is acceptable, and is the poker rate (which requires 6 hours of play per night) acceptable?
questions.known: Venetian publishes a poker rate from $119/$209 that requires six hours of live cash play or a $300+ tournament buy-in per night, or the rate reverts to the prevailing rate.
questions.missing: Whether the player can meet the six-hour condition on every night, and whether a 4-star or 5-star floor is required.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a star floor and decide whether to book the poker rate or the public rate.

questions.question: Is a 10:00 AM start acceptable, given that no 8 AM tournament exists?
questions.known: Earliest verified start is 10:00 AM (Caesars Palace) / 10:10 AM (Venetian). Horseshoe shows 9:00 AM on an editorial page only.
questions.missing: Whether the 8 AM requirement is a hard constraint.
questions.how_to_close: Accept 10 AM, or verify Horseshoe's 9 AM slot directly with the room.

questions.question: Does the Venetian/Venetian-Palazzo poker room publish a maximum-entry rule anywhere not yet read?
questions.known: 14 of 37 DSE IV structure sheets were read in full and none states an entry cap.
questions.missing: 23 structure sheets unread; no Venetian tournament-rules page could be found (the /tournament-rules.html path returns 404).
questions.how_to_close: Read the remaining 23 sheets, or ask lv_cas_poker@venetianlasvegas.com in writing.
questions.affects: Whether any event can ever be marked single-entry

questions.question: What is the all-in entry cost per event, including staff gratuities that buy chips?
questions.known: Fee splits are verified for 14 Venetian sheets, 6 Wynn WPT events, all four Caesars Palace dailies, all four Wynn dailies and both Bellagio weeklies.
questions.missing: Several Bellagio and MGM Grand events attach a *voluntary* gratuity that buys extra chips. Whether to count that as part of the entry cost is an open modelling choice, since not paying it puts you at a chip disadvantage.
questions.how_to_close: Decide whether 'entry cost' means the mandatory minimum or the cost of a competitive stack (mandatory + gratuity).
questions.affects: True cost per event, ranking ratio

questions.question: Is the published guarantee actually reachable in the field sizes these events draw?
questions.known: Guaranteed pool and prize-pool-per-entry are both known for most events, so the number of entries needed to fund the guarantee can be computed exactly.
questions.missing: Actual field sizes are not published before the event. No historical attendance was retrieved.
questions.how_to_close: Use the computed 'entries needed to fund the guarantee' as the comparison, and check the property's published results pages for past field sizes.

questions.question: What does a room actually cost for the chosen dates, all-in?
questions.known: Resort fees are $50–$55 plus tax at every property that publishes one; the Clark County room tax is 13.38% on the Venetian page.
questions.missing: Every dated room rate. Booking engines return placeholders to a non-browser client.
questions.how_to_close: Capture a checkout total in a browser for the chosen dates and occupancy, and record the rate timestamp.

questions.question: Do the walk times hold at the actual times of day, and from the actual hotel tower?
questions.known: Google Maps walking times were measured for 14 hotel→room pairs on 2026-11-16.
questions.missing: Times are point-to-point and measured at one moment; they exclude in-building walking and do not account for crowd levels.
questions.how_to_close: Add 5–10 minutes per walk and re-measure on arrival.

questions.question: Which event should be the primary on each day, given that a long 1-day event blocks an evening event?
questions.known: Venetian 1-day structures run up to 28 levels at 30 minutes plus seven 15-minute breaks, i.e. a derived ceiling of 15 h 45 min from the 11:10 AM start.
questions.missing: Actual finish times and field sizes.
questions.how_to_close: Treat the day plan's 'conditional fallback' as contingent on a bust before the fallback's late-registration close, and check the close time on the day.

questions.question: Does the Bellagio and MGM Grand 'voluntary' gratuity change the effective rake?
questions.known: Bellagio $40 gratuity buys +15,000 (Fri) or +20,000 (Sat) chips on top of 30,000/40,000. MGM Grand $11 buys +10,000 on top of 15,000.
questions.missing: Whether declining the gratuity is realistic in a competitive field.
questions.how_to_close: Model entry cost twice: minimum and with-gratuity.

suggestions.title: Trip-cost calculator
suggestions.what: A live calculator: (selected entries × buy-ins) + (nights × true nightly hotel cost) + parking days.
suggestions.why: Answers 'what does this trip cost' directly instead of leaving it as a formula in prose.
suggestions.how: trip-cost page; hotel inputs default to the published resort fee + Clark County tax and the published starting poker rate, all labelled as such.

suggestions.title: Dated rate log instead of one rate value
suggestions.what: Every rate observation is a row with its own log date, basis, occupancy and source.
suggestions.why: A single 'rate' field silently overwrites history and hides whether a number is a quote or a starting rate.
suggestions.how: rates page reads data/poker/rates.json; nothing is overwritten.

suggestions.title: 'Last checked' on every row
suggestions.what: Every table row shows the date its source was last read.
suggestions.why: A schedule with no date on it is indistinguishable from a current one.
suggestions.how: Every row renders its source-link date (2026-11-16) next to the source link.

suggestions.title: One page per venue
suggestions.what: Venetian, Wynn, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, MGM Grand and Horseshoe each get a page with their events, hotel terms and walk times.
suggestions.why: The decision 'where do I stay' is per-venue, and a mixed table makes it hard to see one property's whole picture.
suggestions.how: venues/*.html generated from the same data.

suggestions.title: Search + date + single-entry toggle
suggestions.what: Free-text search across every table, a date picker, a venue filter and a single-entry-only toggle.
suggestions.why: Requested directly; also the only way to answer 'what can I play on Dec 7' in one action.
suggestions.how: Client-side filter on the events table; the single-entry toggle returns zero rows by design and says why.

suggestions.title: Schedule-overlap flags
suggestions.what: Each day is shown as one primary event plus a conditional fallback, never two 'confirmed' events.
suggestions.why: No source publishes finish times, so a second same-day tournament is never a certainty.
suggestions.how: Derived maximum length from the published structure; a second event is only a fallback if its late-registration close is after the primary's derived ceiling.

suggestions.title: Walking matrix with a 30-minute test
suggestions.what: A hotel→room table with measured minutes, distance, and a pass/fail against 30 minutes.
suggestions.why: Requested directly; also the constraint that removes MGM Grand from a Venetian-based stay.
suggestions.how: 14 pairs measured on Google Maps on 2026-11-16 and recorded with that caveat.

suggestions.title: Automated URL re-check + change diff
suggestions.what: A scheduled job that re-fetches every official URL, hashes the relevant text, and marks rows whose source changed.
suggestions.why: Requested directly. Schedules and fees change without notice.
suggestions.how: Not implemented: it needs a GitHub Actions job with outbound network access, a stored hash per source, and a review queue. The repository's own sandbox has outbound access only to GitHub/npm/PyPI, so the check cannot run here.
suggestions.effort: ~1 hour: one workflow file, one hash store, one 'changed' badge on each row.

suggestions.title: Live hotel-rate lookup
suggestions.what: Query each hotel's booking API for the chosen dates and compute true cost automatically.
suggestions.why: Requested directly, and it is the single biggest hole in the dataset.
suggestions.how: Not implemented: the booking flows are JavaScript apps that return placeholders to non-browser clients, and scraping them is against most of these properties' terms. A compliant option is a manual capture form with a timestamp.
suggestions.effort: Depends entirely on whether the properties offer an approved feed.

suggestions.title: Live daily-schedule scraper
suggestions.what: Pull each room's official daily schedule every morning.
suggestions.how: Not implemented for the same network/terms reason as S-09, and because most Strip dailies are published as PDFs whose layout changes between properties.
suggestions.effort: PDF parsing per venue, plus a human check for layout changes.

suggestions.title: Written single-entry confirmation per event
suggestions.what: Replace every 'unverified' label with a written room confirmation, quoted verbatim.
suggestions.why: This is the only thing that can make the single-entry filter return rows.
suggestions.how: Send one email per room naming the events and asking for the maximum-entry and add-on rules. Store each reply verbatim with its date.
suggestions.effort: Human action; cannot be automated from this sandbox.

suggestions.title: Rank only on confirmed cost and guarantee
suggestions.what: Guarantee ÷ entry fee is shown as a descriptive ratio, with a separate 'entries needed to fund the guarantee' column.
suggestions.why: A ratio without the entry count hides whether a guarantee is a real overlay or needs a full field.
suggestions.how: Ranking page shows both; bounty and flight events are labelled separately.

suggestions.title: Consolidate the four dashboards
suggestions.why: Four parallel sites with conflicting numbers is the largest source of confusion in this repository.
suggestions.how: Applied here: the new dashboard replaces them and the old trees are archived under /archive/ with a banner.
suggestions.effort: Done in this session — review the archive before deleting it.
